heard: One star emits a year of solar energy in 20 seconds. This is the pistol star, a blue hypergiant located 25,000 light years away. Astronomer Don Feiger identified the record breaker in the early 1990s using the Hubble Space Telescope. The hypergiant produces at least 1.6 million times more light than our sun. If the pistol star replaced the sun, its surface would extend past the orbit of Mars. This giant stellar winds are 10 billion times stronger than the breeze from our own star. However, thick cosmic dust blocks our view, absorbing almost all of its visible light. Without that dust, the hypergiant would be easily visible to the naked eye at night. A massive hypernova will eventually end the short life of this radiant monster.
